error_desktop_not_found: The Desktop App has wandered off.
error_no_speakers_selected: No speakers have been chosen for the ritual
error_max_sessions: Too many rituals in progress. Dispel one first.
error_capture_denied: The browser politely but firmly refused
error_playback_failed: Playback has failed, for reasons of its own
error_stop_tab_capture_first: Stop the active tab cast before switching to browser capture
error_stop_browser_capture_first: Stop the active browser cast before switching to tab capture
error_server_error: The server is having one of those days
error_wrong_server: That's not the server we're looking for
error_permission_needed: The extension needs your leave to reach that server. Open Options and click Connect.
error_permission_denied: Permission was declined, so the server remains politely out of reach
error_offscreen_unavailable: The extension's audio capture did not start. Try again.
error_unsupported_sample_rate: Your audio hardware speaks an unfamiliar dialect. Try 48kHz or 44.1kHz in system settings.
auto_stop_source_changed: Sonos has been distracted by something else
auto_stop_stream_ended: The stream has concluded its journey
auto_stop_playback_stopped: Playback has decided to take a break
auto_stop_speaker_stopped: The speaker has wandered off mid-sentence
auto_stop_speaker_taken_over: Another caster has claimed this speaker
auto_stop_continuation_failed: The speaker couldn't move on to the next stretch of the cast. Cast again to carry on.
auto_stop_capture_error: Audio capture encountered an unexpected difficulty
auto_stop_process_exited: The browser process has departed unexpectedly
auto_stop_device_disconnected: The audio device has wandered off mid-performance
error_speaker_stop_failed: {{name}} declined to stop. Feel free to try again.
no_speakers_found: The network was searched. The speakers were not forthcoming.
network.speakers_not_responding: The speakers have been located but appear to be giving us the silent treatment. A VPN or firewall is the likely culprit.
network.speakers_unreachable: Your speakers have made themselves scarce. Firewalls and VPNs are the usual suspects.
hint_replace_cast: This will end your current ritual
server_custom_url_hint: For a server on another machine
server_url_hint: Before connecting, the browser will ask, just the once, whether the extension may "read and change your data" at that address. It only wants a word with the server.
audio_mode_custom_desc: For those who know what they're doing
audio_smoothing_hint: One speaker cutting out needs a longer speaker head start; every speaker cutting out at once needs more smoothing. Each step adds that much delay.
audio_smoothing_migrated: Smoothing is now one setting for every mode, so yours changed from {{from}} ms to {{to}} ms.
audio_frame_size_hint: Audio per message from the browser. Larger frames use a little less CPU and add that much delay. They make no difference to the speakers' Wi-Fi.
audio_sample_rate_follows_capture_hint: PCM goes out at the rate the browser captures it, usually 48 kHz.
audio_head_start_value_desktop: {{value}} ms, set in the Thaumic Cast desktop app
audio_head_start_value_server: {{value}} ms, set in your Thaumic Cast server's config
audio_bit_depth_hint: Available bit depths depend on the selected codec
audio_no_codecs_detected: This device lacks the necessary enchantments
version_mismatch_message: Your {{appTypeLabel}} has fallen behind the extension (currently v{{appVersion}}). Update to restore harmony.
version_mismatch_unknown_message: Your app predates this extension and can't report its version. Update to restore harmony.
onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome, Caster
onboarding.welcome.subtitle: A brief orientation before we proceed
onboarding.welcome.body: Thaumic Cast channels audio from your browser to your Sonos speakers. Think of it as a magical conduit, except the magic is networking and the wand is a browser extension.
onboarding.desktop.title: The Desktop App
onboarding.desktop.subtitle: Your local anchor to the speaker realm
onboarding.desktop.found: Excellent. The Desktop App is present and accounted for.
onboarding.desktop.not_found: The Desktop App has not been summoned. It serves as the bridge to your speakers.
onboarding.desktop.download_prompt: You'll need to install it first:
onboarding.desktop.manual_hint: For non-standard ports or remote servers
onboarding.speakers.title: Your Speakers Await
onboarding.speakers.subtitle: Let's see who's listening
onboarding.speakers.none_found: No speakers have made themselves known. Ensure they're powered on.
onboarding.ready.title: The Ritual is Complete
onboarding.ready.subtitle: Your speakers await instruction
onboarding.ready.intro: You can stream audio from up to {{maxStreams}} tabs at once. The universe has limits.
onboarding.ready.performance_body: Best for music. Audio reaches the speakers about a second after the browser plays it: fine for tunes, less so for conducting orchestras. Turn on video sync to keep films in step.
onboarding.ready.battery_warning: Laptops on battery may experience hiccups. Browsers like to save power.
video_sync_description: For when the lips move but the words arrive fashionably late
keep_tab_audible_description: A whisper of sound to keep Chrome from getting ideas about throttling
sync_speakers_description: When casting to multiple speakers, group them for perfectly synchronized playback. May temporarily rearrange your Sonos speaker groupings.
capture_mode_browser_description: Captures all audio from the browser process. Eliminates frame drops but streams all tabs as one source. Requires the desktop app on Windows 10 21H2+.
capture_health_frame_drops_message: The audio doesn't seem to be having a good day. Browser-wide capture often sorts that out.
capture_health_frame_drops_message_no_re: The audio doesn't seem to be having a good day.
speaker_notice_head_start_ran_out: {{name}} cut out: the Wi-Fi stalled for {{stall}} ms, and a {{current}} ms head start lasts {{current}} ms. Set it to {{suggested}} ms.
speaker_notice_head_start_ran_out_draine: {{name}} cut out: the Wi-Fi stalled for {{stall}} ms, and what was left of its {{current}} ms head start did not stretch to it. Set it to {{suggested}} ms.
speaker_notice_head_start_ran_out_off: {{name}} cut out: the Wi-Fi stalled for {{stall}} ms and the speaker head start is off, so nothing had been put by for it. Set it to {{suggested}} ms.
speaker_notice_head_start_close: {{name}} very nearly cut out: a {{stall}} ms Wi-Fi stall left it {{left}} ms of its {{current}} ms head start, which is not a margin. Set it to {{suggested}} ms.
speaker_notice_head_start_close_off: {{name}} very nearly cut out: the Wi-Fi stalled for {{stall}} ms with the speaker head start off, and it got through on what it happened to have. Set it to {{suggested}} ms.
speaker_notice_head_start_no_remedy: {{name}} cut out: the Wi-Fi stalled for {{stall}} ms, which is more than the longest head start can cover, and that makes it a matter of furniture. Move the speaker nearer the router, or give it an Ethernet cable.
speaker_notice_where_desktop: The speaker head start is in the desktop app, under Settings > Speakers, and a new value takes effect when the speaker next connects, such as when you restart the cast.
speaker_notice_where_server: On the server that setting is pcm_connect_burst_ms, in the config, and a new value takes effect when the speaker next connects, such as when you restart the cast.
speaker_notice_where_fixed: The speaker head start is fixed by THAUMIC_PCM_CONNECT_BURST_MS on the machine where Thaumic Cast runs, and that is the only place it can be changed.
speaker_notice_where_unknown: The speaker head start is set wherever Thaumic Cast runs, and a new value takes effect when the speaker next connects.
speaker_notice_running_low: {{name}} has about {{left}} ms left in reserve, and when that goes, so does the sound.
speaker_notice_running_low_drift: The clock in {{name}} runs a little fast, and that is where the reserve has been going.
speaker_notice_drift_uncorrected: The clock in {{name}} runs a little fast, so it gets through audio quicker than audio arrives, and will run low in about {{minutes}} min.
speaker_notice_drift_saturated: The clock in {{name}} is further out than clock drift correction is permitted to correct, so it will run low in about {{minutes}} min.
speaker_notice_drift_turn_on_desktop: Turn on clock drift correction in the desktop app, under Settings > Speakers; it starts work when the speaker next connects.
speaker_notice_drift_turn_on_server: Set drift_compensation to on in the server's config; it starts work when the speaker next connects.
speaker_notice_restart_refills: Stop the cast and start it again; that refills the reserve.
ingest_gaps_message_desktop_one: Audio from this browser reached the desktop app late once in the last minute, and every speaker had a gap to show for it. Raise smoothing to {{suggested}} ms.
ingest_gaps_message_desktop_other: Audio from this browser reached the desktop app late {{count}} times in the last minute, and every speaker had a gap to show for it. Raise smoothing to {{suggested}} ms.
ingest_gaps_message_server_one: Audio from this browser reached the server late once in the last minute, and every speaker had a gap to show for it. Raise smoothing to {{suggested}} ms.
ingest_gaps_message_server_other: Audio from this browser reached the server late {{count}} times in the last minute, and every speaker had a gap to show for it. Raise smoothing to {{suggested}} ms.
ingest_gaps_no_remedy_desktop: Audio from this browser reached the desktop app up to {{worst}} ms late, and smoothing does not stretch that far. A busy or sleeping computer does this, and so does Wi-Fi between this browser and the app. Give the computer less to do, or a cable.
ingest_gaps_no_remedy_server: Audio from this browser reached the server up to {{worst}} ms late, and smoothing does not stretch that far. Connect this computer or the server by Ethernet.
